gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Notebookcheck measured only 27 hours of battery life on the Keychron K3 HE with backlighting on, against Keychron's 55-hour claim, or that the K3 HE double-typed at 0.2 mm actuation with 0.1 mm Rapid Trigger and stopped only at 0.3 mm.
standout_why: I read three uncited top results in full. Geek Gaming Tricks (published 2026-10-28, updated 2026-10-31) and MKB Guide (published 2026-09-30, updated 2026-10-11) both repeat Keychron's 'up to 55 hours' for the K3 HE. Neither gives a tested runtime, and neither reports K3 HE double inputs at low actuation. Gaming Review Guide (2026-10-04) does not cover the K3 HE and says it does no testing of its own. Geek Gaming Tricks gives no RTINGS numbers. MKB Guide gives none either. I could not read the bodies of the cited RTINGS low-profile list or the Tom's Hardware wireless list: the fetcher returned only the page title or navigation. So I cannot rule out that one of them has a K3 HE battery test, though RTINGS's list is about switch type and latency rather than battery.
decides: This qualifies ChatGPT's #2 pick, the K3 HE as 'best wireless magnetic option' at $119.99. With RGB on, expect about a day of play (27 h) per charge, not 55 h. Competitive FPS players also cannot use its shortest settings (0.2 mm actuation, 0.1 mm Rapid Trigger) without double inputs, so the usable floor is 0.3 mm. That supports ChatGPT's choice of the wired NuPhy Air75 HE for competitive FPS. The K3 HE stays the wireless value pick, with that caveat.

findings.label: Battery life with backlighting on, Notebookcheck test
findings.value: 27 h (tested), against 55 h claimed with no backlight
findings.source_title: Keychron K3 HE review: Low-profile magnetic keyboard punches way above its weight class (Notebookcheck, Julian van der Merwe)
findings.note: Review published 2026-06-05 and updated 2026-10-05. Notebookcheck writes '55 hours with no backlight (claimed); 27 hours with backlighting enabled (tested)'.

findings.label: Battery drain per hour at maximum backlight, Notebookcheck
findings.note: 100 / 3.6 ≈ 27.8 h, which matches the 27 h tested runtime. Drain was measured with backlighting at maximum.

findings.label: Lowest setting free of double inputs, Notebookcheck
findings.value: Double inputs at 0.2 mm actuation with 0.1 mm Rapid Trigger; fixed at 0.3 mm actuation and 0.3 mm Rapid Trigger
findings.note: Notebookcheck says raising actuation and Rapid Trigger sensitivity to 0.3 mm 'resolved this completely'. Keychron's store lists the actuation range as 0.2–2.9 mm.

findings.label: Front height, Notebookcheck
findings.value: 20.5 mm with keycaps; 16.1 mm without keycaps
findings.note: Listed in the review's dimensions (320 × 122 mm). The rival pages give about 22 mm, which they attribute to Keychron. The Keychron store text I read gives only 318.62 × 126 mm and no height.
